sentences.text: By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.26 of 2024 at Police Station-Sahar, District-Auraiya under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in jail since 21.02.2024.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 06.03.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Rajeev Kumar Saxena, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Virendra Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the informant and Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 14 years and 6 months in the F.I.R.
only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no lawful basis for the age related entry of the victim in the school records.
The school records disclosing her age as 14 years and 6 months are unreliable.
(iii) The victim in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is 16 and 14 years of age respectively.
(iv). The medical report drawn up to determine the age of the victim opines that she is 19 years of age.
The victim is a major.

3. The incident occurred on 12.02.2024 and the F.I.R. was got registered on 15.02.2024.
4. Delay of 3 days in lodgement of the F.I.R. in the facts of this case is fatal to the prosecution case.
5. The victim and the applicant were intimate.
6. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship with the applicant.
7. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant and that she eloped with him.

The victim has stated that she got married to the applicant in Balaji Durvesh @ Dhurvesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145773816/
2 Mandir at Jaipur.

sentences.text: Lastly the victim has also asserted that she had consensual physical relations with the applicant.
8. The victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she left for Jaipur after due family discord and after being upbraided by her family members.
The victim has also stated that she stayed with her brother at Jaipur in a hotel and has not got married.

9. The victim has not made any allegation of commission of rape, wrongful detention or forceful assault against the applicant in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C.
10.
The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at public places.
She did not raise an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
Her conduct shows that she was a consenting party.
11. Major inconsistencies in the statements of the victim under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C., as well as the recitals in the F.I.R. discredit the prosecution case.
12. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
13. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
14. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.

Shri Virendra Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the informant who is the father of the victim has stated that the families have amicably resolved the issue and decided to get married of the applicant and the victim immediately after enlarging the bail of the applicant.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Durvesh @ Dhurvesh Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

sentences.text: The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
Before parting some observations have to be made in the facts of this case.

The learned trial court has failed to comply with the judgment rendered by this Court in Monish (supra) regarding the manner of consideration of age of the victim in bail applications filed by the accused persons under the POCSO Act.

A copy of this order as well as a copy of the judgment in Monish (supra) shall be provided to the learned District Judge, Auraiya to ensure that the learned trial courts are guided by the law laid down by this Court.
It is clarified that the above observations shall not be construed adversely against any judicial officer.
